title: Django ORM Escape Hatch: .extra() Misuse
learning_objectives: Explain why QuerySet.extra(), .raw() and RawSQL() bypass the ORM's automatic parameterisation
Recognise ORM escape hatches as first-class SQL injection sinks during code review
Craft a UNION SELECT that matches a query's column count and types to exfiltrate another table
Extract a Django superuser's pbkdf2_sha256 password hash from auth_user via injection
flag_hint: POST /solve with field 'hash' set to the exact auth_user.password value for username='root'; on an exact match the JSON response's 'flag' field returns the per-container flag read from the flag file.
inspired_by: Django ORM escape-hatch SQL injection (QuerySet.extra/.raw/RawSQL) and the 'an ORM won't save you' code-review lesson; Django security advisories in the .extra()/.explain() family (CVE-2022-28347, CVE-2022-34265)
